A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 1000. $2 \, \mu\text{s}$ per division would give only $6 \, \mu\text{s}$ for 3 divisions, not $0.006 \, \text{s}$.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 100. $20 \, \mu\text{s}$ per division would give only $60 \, \mu\text{s}$ for 3 divisions, not $6 \, \text{ms}$.

C.explanation: 3 divisions represent $0.006 \, \text{s}$, so one division is $0.002 \, \text{s} = 2 \, \text{ms}$.

D.explanation: Divides the $0.006 \, \text{s}$ by 2 instead of by the 3 horizontal divisions between the adjacent peaks.

hints: Count the horizontal divisions between the centre of the large peak and the centre of the next small peak on the c.r.o. screen.
Use time interval $=$ number of divisions $\times$ time-base setting, with the interval $0.006 \, \text{s} = 6 \, \text{ms}$.
Divide $6 \, \text{ms}$ by the number of divisions you counted to get the time per division and check $\text{ms}$ against $\mu\text{s}$.
walkthrough: Look at the horizontal axis of the trace. The large peak and the next small peak to its right are separated by 3 full divisions.
Recall that for a c.r.o. time-base, elapsed time $=$ horizontal divisions $\times$ time-base setting.
Convert to milliseconds: $0.002 \, \text{s} = 2 \, \text{ms}$, so the setting is $2 \, \text{ms/division}$. This is option C.
